items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: the chords, Gordy on the tuba, or the bass player, you really have to know the tune pretty well.

ctx.x: When you get in a situation, I mean I always felt like the rhythm players, the bass and the guitar and the banjo — how do I put this — you have to know a song better than the horn players. That’s how I felt in that situation. Because horn players can find single notes, they can sort of meander their way through things, but you guys have to play the correct changes and stuff.

Oh yeah that’s very true. The rhythm section, even the drummer. I judge the quality of a drummer by the way that he plays the tune, the accents that he puts in at the right place at the right time. And some drummers are good drummers but they just don’t have a feel for the music or they don’t know the tune. But as far as people who are doing notes, like me, the chords, Gordy on the tuba, or the bass player, you really have to know the tune pretty well. Because if you don’t play the right changes you can throw the…
Well if you have a good bass player or tuba man, and you can rely on them hitting that downbeat note, but if they’re not then it can be hairy.
